responsibilities: Serve as the dedicated data partner for product and product design: join roadmap planning, weigh in on feature scoping, and make sure the right questions are being asked before anything gets built.
Own product analytics instrumentation: audit existing tracking, identify gaps, and work with engineers to close them.
Build and maintain dbt models that serve as the foundation for product, growth, and operational reporting.
Design and maintain dashboards and self-serve tools that help PMs and leadership answer their own questions.
Drive our understanding of engagement, retention, and activation and surface insights that inform product decisions.
Identify leading indicators of product-market fit and help the team track them over time.
Build and maintain scalable data pipelines across our data warehouse, scoped to product and user data.
Collaborate closely with the analytics engineers who own clinical and research data, coordinating on shared infrastructure and data standards without stepping on each other's domains.
Proactively surface data quality issues within the product and growth domain and establish standards that make our data trustworthy.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Proactively surface data quality issues within the product and growth domain and establish standards that make our data trustworthy.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: reliability and quality language recurs — 'builds the infrastructure to measure it reliably', 'clean, documented', 'standards that make our data trustworthy' — against a single speed phrase ('AI tools to move faster').
evidence.domain_risk: Build and maintain scalable data pipelines across our data warehouse, scoped to product and user data.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate: although the company handles regulated health records, this role's scope is explicitly 'scoped to product and user data' with clinical and research data owned by other analytics engineers.
evidence.collaboration_width: product; product design; engineers; PMs and leadership; the analytics engineers who own clinical and research data
evidence.data_team_maturity: You'll also work alongside analytics engineers on the team who own clinical and research data, so collaboration and clear ownership boundaries matter here.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid: a data team already exists with domain splits — 'analytics engineers on the team who own clinical and research data' — and dbt models are in place, but it is still described as 'a small team'.
evidence.jd_authorship: Hands-on experience with Mixpanel, including working with engineers to define and implement event tracking.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Hiring manager: the bullets name the actual instrumentation work and stack — Mixpanel event tracking, 'BigQuery, dbt, Stitch, and Hex' — and specify the ownership boundary against the clinical data team.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Product and product design are your primary stakeholders.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Product: the JD states outright that 'Product and product design are your primary stakeholders', with responsibilities built around funnels, activation, engagement and retention.
evidence.autonomy_level: You'll define what good product analytics looks like at Novellia
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: 'You will be the internal authority on product analytics, set the standard for how we instrument and measure our product' places direction-setting on the role.
evidence.ai_role: Comfortable using AI tools to move faster: writing SQL, exploring data, documenting your work, whatever gets you there.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_user: AI is the candidate's own accelerant for SQL, exploration and documentation, with no expectation of building data foundations for AI systems.
evidence.testing_framing: Proactively surface data quality issues within the product and growth domain and establish standards that make our data trustworthy.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: data quality is a named responsibility bullet with ownership verbs ('surface', 'establish standards'), not a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: establish standards that make our data trustworthy
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: trust in the data appears once, at the end of the responsibilities list, while the dominant framing is product insight and decision-making rather than compliance or regulatory exposure.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: audit existing tracking, identify gaps, and work with engineers to close them
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mixed: the role both defines a new measurement standard ('You'll define what good product analytics looks like at Novellia') and repairs what exists ('audit existing tracking, identify gaps').
evidence.loss_aversion: Risk framing is light and limited to data trust within one domain: 'Proactively surface data quality issues within the product and growth domain and establish standards that make our data trustworthy.'
